title: Improving quantum-battery charging via unidirectional quantum jumps to metastable state
authors: Ewelina Lange, Grzegorz Chimczak, Anna Kowalewska-Kudłaszyk, Kishore Thapliyal, Jan Peřina
abstract: In the process of charging a quantum battery, quantum jumps play a detrimental role because they induce transitions from higher to lower energy levels, leading to energy dissipation. This be- havior directly opposes the fundamental objective of the charging protocol, which is to increase the population of higher-energy states and store usable energy in the system. Furthermore, decoherence introduced by randomness of quantum jumps leads to a mixed state, thereby reducing the amount of energy that can be extracted from the charged quantum battery. Here, we propose a quantum battery comprising an ensemble of three-level atoms in the Λ configuration to store energy in the metastable state over a long time. We demonstrate that, when spontaneous atomic transitions are restricted to occur solely from the excited state to a metastable state, with decay to the ground state completely suppressed, quantum jumps acquire a constructive character. Under these con- ditions, they drive the quantum battery to a fully charged state, render the entire stored energy extractable, and shorten the duration of the second stage of the charging protocol.
summary: The paper proposes using a three-level atomic system configured as a quantum battery to store energy efficiently. By artificially restricting spontaneous decay paths to be unidirectional toward a metastable state, the detrimental effects of quantum jumps are converted into a constructive process that rapidly charges the battery and maximizes extractable energy.
main_problem: Quantum jumps during quantum battery charging cause energy dissipation by inducing transitions from high to low energy states, hindering efficient energy storage.
main_result: Restricting spontaneous atomic transitions to be unidirectional (excited state only decays to metastable state) makes the quantum jumps constructive, driving the system to a fully charged state and making all stored energy extractable.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics using master equations and compare results from full damping models against simpler coherent or non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approaches.
model_or_system: The model uses an ensemble of three-level atoms in a Lambda (Λ) configuration, designed to store energy in a metastable state. The system is coupled to an optical cavity charger.
key_observables: Sum of populations in the metastable states ($\langle P_{n} \sum \sigma^{(j)}_{11} angle$), which serves as the figure of merit for storable energy, and ergotropy (extractable work).
important_parameters: The analysis explores different parameter regimes defined by detunings ($\Delta$) and coupling strengths ($\Omega_i, g, \gamma$).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is the restriction of spontaneous transitions to be unidirectional from the excited state $|2angle$ only to the metastable state $|1angle$, suppressing decay to the ground state $|0angle$.
figures_summary: Figure 3 compares the evolution of stored energy ($\langle P_{n, j=1} \sigma^{(j)}_{11} angle$) over time using three different dynamic descriptions: Hermitian Hamiltonian, non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, and the full Master Equation approach.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem (energy loss via jumps) and proposes a modified $\Lambda$-system. It then develops the theoretical framework by comparing dynamics under various approximations (Hamiltonian vs. Master Equation). Finally, it demonstrates that the unidirectional jump mechanism yields constructive charging behavior.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses energy management in open quantum systems, showing how engineering dissipation pathways (reservoir engineering) can turn a source of loss into a driving force for achieving desired quantum states.
